assumptions.choice: Genetic-algorithm parameter optimization is not implemented; the strategy runs once with the spec's stated default parameters (SMA 20/50, RSI 14, MACD 12/26/9, SMA200 trend filter, ATR14 vol filter, TP 2%/SL 1%, size 2% of free cash).
assumptions.reason: GA-driven multi-run parameter search requires an external optimizer that spawns/evaluates many Cerebro backtests; the harness executes a single bt.Strategy class against one fixed data feed with no ability to launch nested backtests.

assumptions.choice: A plugin system for loading external indicator/rule modules is not implemented.
assumptions.reason: Allowed imports are restricted to backtrader, math, collections, statistics, and the output must be a single self-contained class with no dynamic module loading, so there is no mechanism to attach external plugins.

assumptions.choice: Historical data loading is not implemented in the strategy; it relies entirely on the harness-provided data feed and Cerebro setup.
assumptions.reason: The environment fixes data loading/Cerebro configuration outside the submitted class; a bt.Strategy cannot itself source external historical data here.

assumptions.choice: SMA (not EMA) with periods 20/50 drives the entry/exit crossover logic; EMA(20)/EMA(50) are computed and available but do not drive trades.
assumptions.reason: The spec's explicit default naming ('SMA 20, SMA 50') identifies SMA as the default MA type; the generic 'moving average crosses' entry/exit wording is read literally against that named default.

assumptions.choice: EMA fast/slow periods default to 20/50, mirroring the SMA defaults.
assumptions.reason: Spec requires EMA support but gives no EMA-specific default period; reused the stated SMA defaults as the closest literal reading.

assumptions.choice: RSI(14) and MACD(12,26,9) are computed each bar as available indicators but are not wired into entry/exit gating.
assumptions.reason: Spec lists them as part of the indicator toolkit to implement, but the given example entry/exit rules reference only the MA crossover; no additional filter is invented from RSI/MACD.

assumptions.choice: ATR(14) normalized as ATR/Close must fall between 0.5% and 5% for new entries to be allowed.
assumptions.reason: Spec states an ATR-based volatility filter with no explicit low/high threshold values; price-normalized bounds were chosen as a reasonable, declared default since raw ATR is not comparable across price levels.

assumptions.choice: Both filters default to enabled (use_trend_filter=True, use_vol_filter=True) via toggleable params.
assumptions.reason: Spec frames these as filters that can be enabled to improve signal quality; defaulting to enabled reflects that intent while remaining toggleable per the spec's 'ability to enable' phrasing.

assumptions.choice: Size = position_size_pct * broker.getcash() / close price, floored to whole shares.
assumptions.reason: 'Free capital' is read literally as uncommitted cash rather than total equity; share count is floored since AAPL trades in whole shares.

assumptions.choice: TP (2%) and SL (1%) are evaluated against each bar's closing price in next(); the risk-management section's stop-loss is treated as the same single 1% level, not a second mechanism.
assumptions.reason: The exit-conditions and risk-management sections both cite a 1% stop-loss; treating them as one avoids inventing a duplicate stop. Evaluating against bar close is the simplest literal reading given only OHLCV bars and next()-based logic.
